decisions.quote:
Neonatal imitation: Two failures to replicate
Jean E. Koepke, Marilyn Hamm, Maria Legerstee, Mary Russell
Abstract
The purpose of the present research was to replicate two experiments in which neonatal imitation was reported. In replicating the first experiment tongue- and lip-protrusion, mouth-opening, and sequential finger movement were modeled for six 2-week-old babies. Judgments of which models the babies were probably watching and trying to imitate were made from video-tape records of their behavior. In replicating the second experiment mouth-opening and tongue-protrusion were modeled for 14 babies 17- to 21-days-old. Videotape records of their behavior were scored for frequency of imitative behaviors. In replicating the first experiment a potential for experimenter bias that was inherent in the procedure was eliminated and in replicating the second the reliability of the scoring procedure, limited to within scorer originally, was extended to include between scorer as well. The results of both replications failed to yield evidence of neonatal imitation and thus raise questions a
decisions.reason: The recovered complete1977Science article at319positively supplies both source-described experiments: first the four facial/manual gesture models in six neonates and video judgments, second mouth-opening/tongue-protrusion frequency scoring with within-observer reliability. Current abstract independently describes those two experiments and specific bias/reliability extensions. This compound procedural/finding fingerprint, the exact published citation and full primary original establish the unique positively fitting report under Step2description rule. Jacobson1979primary evidence concerns older infants and different stimuli. UnrecoveredHayes1981and earlier1975/1976Meltzoffreports do not supply positive evidence of a different equally fitting tested pair; do not demand an impossible exclusion of hypothetical unseen reports or explicit current in-text citation when description is diagnostic. Prefer the complete published1977report over earlier presentation/thesis accounts, without claiming every report/cohort identical. Both experiments are one original paper, not two missing originals. Bind existing319; current-body absence and unrecovered alternate-report details remain recorded, but do not negate this positive identity.

decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent; the prior expert review returned undeterminable before reference and original-reprint recovery. The current source (592d372d41a77ec8.txt) remains the abstract plus six deposited references. The abstract describes replicating two experiments reporting neonatal imitation: Experiment 1 modeling tongue protrusion, lip protrusion, mouth opening, and sequential finger movement for six 2-week-old infants with video judgments of which model the baby was imitating while eliminating an inherent experimenter bias; and Experiment 2 modeling mouth opening and tongue protrusion for 14 17- to 21-day-old infants with video frequency scoring while extending reliability from within-scorer to between-scorer. The verified 4-page reprint of Meltzoff & Moore (1977, bib4, 10.1126/science.198.4312.75, 21_meltzoff_original.raw.unrepaired.txt) reports both exact experiments: Experiment 1 (six 12- to 17-day-old neonates, those exact four facial/manual gestures, video rank judgments collapsed to yes/no, and an explicitly noted readministration/prefiltering bias on p. 77) and Experiment 2 (12 16- to 21-day-old neonates, mouth opening and tongue protrusion, video frequency tallies, and intraobserver-only reliability in Note 5). Among the other five references, bib1 (Cochran, 1950), bib5 (Piaget, 1962), and bib6 (Uzgiris, 1975) are statistics/theory works, bib3 (Jacobson, 1979) studied 6- to 14-week-old infants with pen/ball/ring releasers, and bib2 (Hayes, 1981, HTTP 403) is a subsequent artifact critique. Under the codebook's description rule, target_index 0 binds to shipped row 319 (shipped_right), while preserving that the current text is abstract-only and no second unshipped original paper is established.
